title: MEXC Users Put Nearly a Third of First-Month RealStocks Volume Into SpaceX
author: Mexc
description: MEXC's RealStocks platform, which launched June 1st offering access to 7,000+ US stocks and ETFs, reported strong first-month trading insights. SpaceX dominated with 29.70% of trading volume, while seven AI-related assets collectively captured 23.67% of volume. The platform attracted over 120,000 users in its first month, with more than 40% of volume distributed outside the top 10 holdings, indicating portfolio-building behavior rather than speculative trading.

title: Down 34% From Its Highs, Is Marvell Technology a Buy on the Dip?
author: Keithen Drury
description: Marvell Technology has declined 34% from its all-time high, prompting questions about whether it's a good buying opportunity. However, the article argues that Broadcom is a superior investment choice, offering higher growth projections (66-63% vs 41-45%), better client relationships with more aggressive AI chip orders, and lower valuation despite its larger size and stronger outlook.

title: Is Marvell Technology the New Nvidia?
author: Keithen Drury
description: While Marvell Technology has emerged as a strong AI investment candidate with major clients Amazon and Microsoft for custom AI chips, the article argues it may not be the better buy compared to Nvidia and Broadcom. Despite solid 41-45% expected revenue growth, Marvell trades at a premium valuation while Broadcom offers faster growth (66-63%) at lower valuations, and Nvidia has similar next-year growth prospects at less than half Marvell's price.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While Marvell has strong fundamentals with major clients (Amazon, Microsoft) and solid 41-45% growth expectations, the article concludes it's overvalued relative to competitors with similar or better growth prospects at lower prices.

Nvidia offers superior valuation (less than half Marvell's price) with similar next-year growth expectations (42%), strategic positioning in AI infrastructure, and a $2 billion investment in Marvell demonstrates confidence in the broader AI ecosystem.

Broadcom is positioned as the better alternative to Marvell, offering faster expected growth (66-63%) in the same custom AI chip industry at significantly lower valuations, with major clients including Alphabet, Meta, OpenAI, and Anthropic.

title: Marvell Technology vs. Nvidia: What Do the Revenue Trends of These Artificial Intelligence Companies Tell Investors?
author: Robert Izquierdo
description: Nvidia and Marvell Technology have both experienced consistent quarter-over-quarter revenue growth driven by AI sector demand. Nvidia's revenue reached $81.6 billion in Q2 2026, demonstrating its dominance in AI semiconductors with a 34x revenue gap over Marvell's $2.4 billion. While Nvidia shows accelerating expansion, Marvell functions as an AI infrastructure 'picks and shovels' player with steady growth, recently added to the S&P 500.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Nvidia demonstrates exceptional revenue acceleration with Q2 2026 revenue of $81.6 billion, showing consistent quarter-over-quarter growth. The company's 66% EBIT margin and central role in the AI ecosystem, evidenced by partnerships like the Japanese government's national AI infrastructure project, indicate strong market dominance and customer demand.

Marvell shows consistent quarter-over-quarter revenue growth from $1.3 billion to $2.4 billion over eight quarters, demonstrating solid demand for its data infrastructure solutions. Recent addition to the S&P 500 and 52-week high of $329.88 in June indicate positive market recognition, though its smaller scale reflects its supporting role in the AI infrastructure ecosystem.

title: AI Infrastructure Will Mint More Millionaires Over the Next Decade: 3 Stocks to Buy Right Now
author: Leo Sun
description: The global AI infrastructure market is projected to expand at 26.6% CAGR through 2034. Three infrastructure leaders—Marvell, Coherent, and Vertiv—are positioned to capitalize on this growth through connectivity chips, fiber-optic components, and cooling systems respectively. All three stocks show strong EBITDA growth projections and are considered reasonably valued relative to their long-term potential.

Leading photonics company experiencing strong demand as data centers replace copper with fiber-optic cables. Expected 44% EBITDA CAGR through 2028 reflects robust growth prospects in AI infrastructure.

Provides critical thermal management and cooling solutions for high-powered AI chips. Co-developing infrastructure with Nvidia and projecting 38% EBITDA CAGR through 2028, indicating solid growth trajectory.
